Invalid initial direct-service comparison: randomUUID may start with a digit, unlike SEWN NewId; 9/36 JSON and 10/36 SQLite create/query sequences succeeded. All queries succeeded, but reduced writes make latency incomparable. No deadline failure.
retainedAnomalies.correction: Use w + UUID without hyphens, exactly as SEWN does; regression tests require both services and reported commits.

retainedAnomalies.result: Earlier CLI prints zero deadline exhaustions for disabled windows because there are no private traces. Actual category is unknown; evidence uses null. CLI corrected; client 500/indeterminate is retained without claiming a privately metered match.
61/64: actual alpha.25 startup banners differed from three stale alpha.24 regexes; corrected after inspecting output; same command passed 64/64

0/1 regression before correction: incomplete response with committed header and diagnostics disabled was classified committed. Corrected to indeterminate; focused 51/51 passes. All 580 measured POST responses were complete, so retained experiment outcomes are unaffected.

finalRequiredRepeat: Required npm test / npm run check run after this evidence update; actual results are retained in the delivery commit message and final report.
limitations: One process contains both HTTP clients and server per fresh window; client timings include shared-process scheduling. No other test suite ran during measurement.

Actual Page overlap is reconstructed from Date-clock ledger anchors and final elapsed at 1ms resolution; clock jumps can distort it. Native-service controls omit Page adaptation and are distinguishing experiments, not the same HTTP workload.
50ms sampler final tails are incomplete; missing samples are not evidence of zero delay. Callback lateness does not identify JS, GC, OS scheduling or other causes.

Largest observed unchecked gap is conservative. A largest checkpoint with checks is not an unchecked interval. Counters and service spans overlap across requests and phases; do not subtract them for CPU/exclusive time.

Native stages aggregate fixed per-request elapsed intervals. JSON work includes asynchronous storage/preflight/cleanup; queue timing is actual enqueue-to-dequeue. SQLite preflight includes awaited filesystem/lifecycle checks and continuation delays; transaction includes synchronous open/setup/transaction/close. None is a disk or CPU measurement.
Completed native stages include rejected/thrown settlements, not only successful service results. Reported commits do not prove client receipt or universal durability reporting.
These bounded single-host measurements establish a matching failure class and delay locations, not the original historical cause, a production concurrency limit, a provider defect or a mitigation.
